title: Find the First Position of a Value
oneLiner: Linear search: walk the list with an index and return the first position holding the target, or -1 if it isn't there.
keyTakeaway: Return from inside the loop the moment you find a match; the code after the loop only runs when nothing matched, so that's where the "not found" answer goes. This is linear search, O(n), what IndexOf and list.index do inside.
explanation:
Return the index of the first element equal to the target, or -1 if the target isn't in the list. Write the loop yourself rather than calling Array.IndexOf or list.index (which, in Python, raises ValueError when the value is missing instead of returning -1).

You need the position, not just the value, so loop by index: for (int i = 0; i < nums.Length; i++) in C#, for i in range(len(nums)) or for i, n in enumerate(nums) in Python. When nums[i] equals the target, return i straight away: that's what makes it the first match. If the loop finishes without returning, the value wasn't there, so return -1 after the loop.

This is linear search: in the worst case it looks at every element, O(n). If the list were sorted you could do much better with binary search, O(log n); see the Binary Search lesson in the Patterns track.

visualizationSteps.message: Index 0 holds 12: not it, keep going.
Index 1 holds 30: return 1 right now. The second 30 at index 3 is never even looked at.
If the target were 99, the loop would check all five and finish without returning, so the line after the loop returns -1.

complexity.note: Linear search: the worst case (target missing or last) checks all n elements; only the index is stored.
